rules.text: The spinner shows no words: name what's loading, and add a short line of text next to it when the wait is more than a moment.

rules.text: For example, a spinner named “Loading your statements” and one line that says the same: “Fetching your statements…”.

rules.text: Say what's loading: a short line next to it tells people what they're waiting for.

rules.text: Don't leave it unexplained: a spinner on its own says something is happening, not what.

examples.purpose: Refreshing statements, the guide's In context, while they load: the list under the title is swapped for a 40 px spinner named “Loading your statements” and one line of text, and the list comes back when the statements arrive. The screen owns the loading state; Refresh is off while it loads, as in the guide's own example. The literal disabled and the empty onPress stand for the screen's own state and wiring.
examples.jsx:
<VStack>
  <Title title="Statements" subtitle="Savings account ··4821" />
  <VStack alignHorizontal="center">
    <Spinner size={40} accessibilityLabel="Loading your statements" />
    <Text text="Fetching your statements…" />
  </VStack>
  <Button label="Refresh" disabled onPress={() => {}} />
</VStack>

from.quote: Refresh swaps the list for a spinner and a line of text while the statements load, then brings the list back.

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: The name of the root, a progressbar (“Loading” by default). There is no value, aria-busy or live region. Declared: Accessibility label announced to assistive tech. Defaults to "Loading". Default "Loading", from the component source.

props.name: size
props.description: The diameter, with no clamp; the arc stroke is 12.8 / 72 of it (12.8 px at 72). Declared: Diameter in px. The spinner is always rendered at a 1:1 ratio, so a single size controls both width and height. Defaults to the Figma size (72). Default 72, from the component source.

props.name: durationMs
props.description: Duration of one full clockwise revolution of the leading segment, in ms. Lower = faster. Defaults to 1500. Default 1500, from the component source.

props.name: gravity
props.description: Default 0.45, clamped to 0–0.9; 0 gives an even speed. Declared: "Weightiness" of the fall, in `[0, 0.9]`. 0 = perfectly constant speed; higher values make segments whip faster over the top and ease through the bottom. Kept below 1 so the motion never reverses. Defaults to 0.45. Default 0.45, from the component source.

props.name: colors
props.description: { primary, secondary, tertiary }: the leading gold arc (primary, drawn on top), then the purple and the teal. Declared: Override any subset of the token-driven segment colours.

props.name: animating
props.description: false, or reduced motion on the device, shows the resting fan. Reduced motion comes from prefers-reduced-motion on the web, and no prop overrides it. Declared: When false, renders a static resting spinner (also honoured for reduced motion). Defaults to true. Default true, from the component source.

props.name: modes
props.description: Has no effect on the output: no mode collection changes the spinner; only colors does. Declared: Design token modes forwarded to token lookups.

props.name: ...SpinnerBaseProps
props.description: Inherited React Native props the component also accepts. They are not part of the design contract and no guide documents them.

gaps.text: The published Storybook page is still the old generated one.
Figma's Spinner is one static pose (contiguous arcs, a ~69° gap); the code's resting pose is three separate arcs 120° apart.
